extracted.intended_audience: Authors and researchers submitting to Nature Portfolio journals, institutional press officers, and journalists covering Nature content
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher policy guidance on media communications, press releases, embargoes, and researcher/journalist conduct around papers submitted to or accepted by Nature Portfolio journals. Covers permitted preprint/conference communication and rules for timing, distribution, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author solicitation of media for submitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions. Authors who wish to publicise their work should coordinate with the journal press office and follow embargo rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and scope of permitted discussion (post-acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions may be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date, subject to the journal's embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion before this window is discouraged; authors may arrange their own publicity but must strictly adhere to the media embargo and are advised to coordinate publicity with the journal press office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases distribution and journalist access
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature produces and distributes press releases summarising upcoming content to a list of registered journalists, who are encouraged to read the full papers they wish to cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists receive names and contact details of corresponding authors and access to the full text about a week before publication via a password‑protected website, together with other relevant material (e.g., News and Views, extra images). The press release and the papers are embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection and highlighting of newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers deemed especially newsworthy may be highlighted by a brief summary on the journal's press release, written by editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this time authors may receive media inquiries and are encouraged to cooperate with journalists so coverage is accurate and balanced. Editors and press office coordinate which papers are summarised or prioritised for press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' independent publicity must respect embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may arrange their own publicity (for instance through institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to the journal's media embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to coordinate their own publicity activities with the journal press office to avoid premature disclosure and to ensure consistency with the embargoed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of embargo (fair access and reliance on peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo policy aims to release information in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media and allows informed comment based on the complete and final published paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes support journalists' ability to obtain independent reactions and rely on peer review; premature release denies that confidence and may preclude balanced coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for breaking embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break embargoes may be removed from the press‑release circulation list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Portfolio journals reserve the right to remove journalists who break embargoes and will continue to use this sanction when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations do not constitute prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio supports open communications between researchers and states that neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may display drafts on established preprint servers before or during submission; exposure of preprints does not preempt submission to Nature journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media responses to preprints and conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to media requests about preprints or conference presentations by providing explanation, clarification, or contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When doing so, researchers should make it clear the paper has not yet undergone peer review and that findings are provisional; such media coverage will not hinder editorial handling but may reduce or pre‑empt media coverage at the time of formal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of peer review and editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to keep details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose reviewer reports or confidential editorial deliberations; public discussion should focus on the research itself and, for preprints, state provisional status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for journalists covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters who cover preprints are recommended to clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit statements in coverage noting provisional status and the absence of peer review to avoid misleading the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact point for clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: If further clarification about press and embargo policy is required, contact the Nature Portfolio press office by e‑mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors, institutions, and journalists should use the press office as the authoritative source for timing, embargo details, and coordination.
